documents.title: About the Institute of Information Management
documents.text: IIM describes itself as an international professional, membership-driven institute focused on data and information management and related disciplines. It serves professionals working with data, information, records, documents, knowledge, content and archives across public and private organisations. Its activities include professional membership, certification, training, continuing professional development, research/publications, seminars, workshops and conferences.

documents.title: IIM Mission and Vision
documents.text: IIM states that its mission is to help information-management professionals remain current with challenges involving information assets, technology and compliance while maintaining standards in certification, competence, research and member value. Its vision is to be recognised as a leading information-management institution in Africa and to influence professional and educational standards in data and information management.

documents.title: IIM International Presence
documents.text: According to IIM's Nigeria About page, IIM is headquartered in Colorado, USA and has chapters or presence in locations including the UK, Canada, South Africa, Australia, Switzerland, India, Ghana and Nigeria.

documents.title: IIM Registration and Approval Claims
documents.text: According to IIM's official website, IIM is a Colorado nonprofit corporation (Entity ID 20181786160). The site states that it operates as a registered professional body in Nigeria with CAC registration RC 1125723 and cites Federal Ministry of Education reference FME/TED/A&E/ANPB/XLIII/406. The site also states that IIM is licensed by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) to conduct examinations and certify data-protection professionals under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. Formal legal or recognition claims should be presented as statements from IIM's official website unless primary approval documents are supplied by the client.

documents.title: Nigeria Membership Categories and Grades
documents.text: IIM lists Student, Individual and Corporate membership categories. Nigeria individual grades progress through Student Member (STIIM), Graduate Member (GMIIM), Associate Member (AMIIM), Professional Member (PMIIM), Senior Professional Member (SPMIIM) and Fellow Member (FIIM). Corporate Member uses CORMIIM. Membership applications are subject to IIM approval and active membership requires applicable fees.

documents.title: Nigeria Membership Grade Eligibility
documents.text: Student Member is for full-time students in information management or related professional courses, with proof of active study. Graduate Member is for recent graduates and the site says candidates should complete IIM membership pre-induction training before induction. Associate Member is an early-career grade with qualification/experience or prescribed upgrade routes. Professional Member can be reached through degree/HND/OND plus experience routes, recognised IIM professional/master certification, or other qualifications approved by the Membership Committee. Senior Professional Member is for senior professionals with supervisory responsibility, relevant qualifications and substantial post-graduation experience. Fellow Member is IIM's senior grade based on eminence, authority and/or seniority; the page commonly cites about 15 years of IM/IT specialist experience and committee/council approval. Corporate membership is for organisations/government establishments and the page states that the organisation should have at least five employees and provide supporting corporate details.

documents.title: Nigeria Membership Fees
documents.text: Nigeria membership fees shown on IIM's official Grades page on 13 August 2026 were: Student - registration exempt, annual subscription USD 50; Graduate - registration exempt, one-time induction USD 60, annual subscription USD 100; Associate - registration USD 100, induction USD 66, annual subscription USD 110; Professional - registration USD 100, induction USD 99, annual subscription USD 180; Senior Professional - registration USD 100, induction USD 134, annual subscription USD 200; Fellow - registration USD 100, induction USD 173, annual subscription USD 242; Corporate - registration USD 100, induction USD 237, annual subscription USD 245. The page states that membership payments are non-refundable. These fees are time-sensitive and should be rechecked before production or if a later review date is reached.

documents.title: Membership Benefits
documents.text: IIM membership benefits described on the official site include participation in regular, general and special meetings for members in good standing; receiving meeting notices and programme information; eligibility for relevant governance/election participation subject to membership rules; special consideration for seminars, conferences and workshops; access to IIM information resources; and professional development, networking and recognition opportunities.

documents.title: Membership Upgrade
documents.text: Existing IIM members may use continuing professional development and professional activities toward a membership upgrade, subject to IIM requirements. Activities listed include courses/conferences, publications, teaching/tutoring, examination work, relevant projects/consultancy and passing an IIM membership-upgrade examination. Current subscription should be paid before submitting an upgrade application. The page displayed an upgrade fee of NGN 30,000 or USD 150 when reviewed on 13 August 2026. Fellow upgrades remain subject to Membership Committee recommendation and Governing Council ratification. The fee should be treated as dynamic.

documents.title: IIM Certification Framework
documents.text: IIM describes its professional certifications as competence pathways in data and information management. The framework includes a foundation stage for candidates who do not yet meet professional examination requirements, compulsory Information Management Professional (IMP) Stage I, Stage II and Stage III, and master/specialist certifications. The website lists examples such as CDPP, CDPO-Compliance, PDPS, CDPCO, CRIMP, CHIMP, CDMP, CISP, CGISP, CAMP, CDBMP, CDOMP, CKMP and CLMP.

documents.title: General Certification Process
documents.text: IIM states that candidates generally attend pre-certification training, either online or classroom, before testing unless an exemption applies. Applications and supporting credentials are reviewed before examination eligibility is approved. Education and professional experience/portfolio evidence may be considered in exemption or assessment pathways where IIM criteria are met. IIM states that certification examinations are open to registered members and non-members. The general certification page displayed a non-refundable USD 16 application-processing fee when reviewed on 13 August 2026; this amount is dynamic. Exam-fee refunds may apply only under stated cancellation conditions and with an administration deduction, so exact current refund terms should be confirmed before quoting them.

documents.title: Certified Data Protection Officer (CDPO)
documents.text: IIM's Certified Data Protection Officer (CDPO) certification is designed to validate competence in data protection and privacy, including compliance, governance, data protection impact assessments (DPIAs), breach/risk management and organisational compliance support. The official page states that the programme is aligned with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and references GDPR, the Malabo Convention, Convention 108+ and ISO/IEC 27701.

documents.title: CDPO Eligibility
documents.text: The CDPO page lists eligibility routes including at least two years of experience in data protection, compliance or information security; completion of IIM-accredited DPO training; or a relevant IIM-recognised professional certification. Candidate eligibility and any exemptions should still be confirmed through the IIM certification process for the individual applicant.

documents.title: CDPO Process and Examination
documents.text: The CDPO process described by IIM is to register, attend recognised/approved training, register or schedule the examination, pass and satisfy the applicable requirements, then apply for the certificate/digital badge. The official CDPO page describes the exam as 60 questions in 150 minutes with a 70% passing requirement. Knowledge areas include legal/regulatory frameworks, data-protection principles and compliance, risk management and DPIA, incident response/data breaches, and governance/policies/ethics. The page describes CDPO examinations as available through secure remote proctoring worldwide.

documents.title: CDPO Re-Certification
documents.text: The detailed IIM CDPO re-certification SOP states that the CDPO certificate is valid for one year (12 months) and renewal is annual. A minimum of 20 CPD points is required in the certification year. The application window opens 60 days before expiry and the SOP recommends applying at least 30 days before expiry. Required items include CPD evidence/log, the re-certification application, valid identification, professional conduct/compliance declaration and proof of the applicable fee. When reviewed on 13 August 2026, the SOP showed maintenance fees of NGN 50,000 for an IIM Accredited Member and NGN 70,000 for a non-IIM member; these fees are dynamic. The SOP states that applications may be reviewed within five working days and CPD evidence may be audited. Appeals should be submitted in writing to certification@iim-africa.org within 14 days of notification.

documents.title: Expired CDPO Certificate
documents.text: IIM's detailed re-certification SOP says an expired CDPO certificate becomes inactive and use of the CDPO designation should stop until reinstatement. The SOP describes reinstatement conditions that can depend on the length or severity of the lapse, with re-examination possible for severe non-compliance. However, an official FAQ also contains a statement that an expired candidate would have to retake the examination, while elsewhere it says re-examination is not required for renewal when requirements are met within the validity period. Because the official pages are not fully consistent, the chatbot must not promise a single expired-certificate outcome. Advise the user to contact certification@iim-africa.org for a case-specific decision.

documents.title: Continuing Professional Development (CPD/MCPD)
documents.text: IIM describes MCPD/CPD as continuing learning used by information-management professionals to maintain and improve knowledge, skills and professional capability. The Nigeria CPD page states that members are expected to make an annual CPD declaration and lists a minimum of 20 CPD points each year. CPD examples include approved webinars/workshops, conferences/seminars, relevant training, publications/research, professional speaking/facilitation and participation in IIM committees, projects or working groups.

documents.title: Accredited Training Organisations (ATOs)
documents.text: IIM accredits training organisations/providers against criteria covering trainer competence, course content, training methods, facilities or online platforms, quality assurance, data-protection compliance, ethics, reporting and continuous improvement. Accredited organisations may provide IIM-aligned training and CPD support. Providers are periodically evaluated and can lose accreditation for non-compliance. Because provider accreditation-validity dates change, the chatbot should not treat a permanently hard-coded provider list as current; users asking for a current provider should be directed to IIM's live accredited-provider page or the Training/Certification Department.

documents.title: Training and Certification Subject Areas
documents.text: IIM training/certification pages show subject areas including archiving and preservation, archives management, database management, document management, geographic information systems, health information management, information security, knowledge management, library management, records/information management and related data/privacy specialisations.

documents.title: Digital Badges and Certification Verification
documents.text: IIM digital badges are recognition and visibility tools for certifications, membership/fellowship and event/training participation. IIM states that a digital badge is not a substitute for an official certificate or formal verification. Certification or status claims should be verified through official IIM/NDPC verification channels. Badges should only be used while the underlying membership or certification is valid, must not be altered or used to imply regulatory authority, and certification-related badges should not continue to be used after expiry, suspension or withdrawal.

documents.title: IIM Research and Publications
documents.text: IIM publication and research resources listed on the official site include the IIM Journal for Data and Information Management (IIM-JDIM), IM World Magazine and RIM Africa Journal. The website also exposes research, webinars and working-group resources. Issue and volume information changes over time, so users seeking the latest issue should be directed to the current publications page.

documents.title: Consultancy and Organisational Services
documents.text: IIM consultancy and organisational services described on the official website include policy and procedure development, programme support and management, records management and retention-schedule appraisal, business-process modelling, information strategy/governance, consultancy for government and private organisations, certification programmes, awareness/change-management support, and participation in professional and educational initiatives.

documents.title: IIM Data Protection and Privacy Summary
documents.text: IIM's privacy policy describes collection of identity/contact, membership, payment, qualification/exam, MCPD, employment, query/complaint, event/training media and potentially biometric data through membership applications, examination registration, events/training, customer service and some third-party sources. Stated purposes include membership administration, qualification/accreditation records, training/study materials, exams, CPD, support, service improvement, regulatory/disciplinary functions and marketing. The policy allows lawful/necessary sharing with relevant service providers, employers, regulators and legal authorities and states that IIM does not sell personal information. Listed rights include access, withdrawal of consent where applicable, portability in some circumstances, rectification and erasure in specific situations. Privacy/data-processing enquiries can be directed to dpo@iim-africa.org. The website states the policy was last updated 10 February 2025.

documents.title: Events and Conferences
documents.text: IIM runs conferences, conventions, webinars, workshops and other professional events. Event dates, speakers, venues, registration status and costs are time-sensitive and past events remain visible on some IIM pages. The chatbot should not rely on permanently hard-coded event dates. For a current or future event, direct the user to the live IIM event page or the relevant IIM team.

documents.title: Dynamic and Verified Data Handling
documents.text: Fees, event calendars, training dates, provider accreditation validity and live certification status can change. If a stored review date is old or the user asks for a live/current status, the chatbot should say the information may have changed and direct the user to the current IIM website or responsible department. The chatbot must never infer approval, eligibility, certification status or examination outcome for a specific person from general information.
